prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Asset type: redesigned maintenance application concept image for a software developer portfolio. Input image is a reference for real workflow facts, NOT a layout to preserve. Create an exceptional high-fidelity flat desktop product UI at 1920 × 1200, landscape 16:10. Fill the entire image with the application interface, no browser chrome, device frame, perspective, vignette, surrounding marketing words or illustration. Inspired by the usability principles of Asana queue-with-detail and Jobber customer context, without copying either brand. Subject brand "MetroNest", subtitle "Maintenance ops". Render small visible "Sample data" chip at top right. Crisp readable elegant sans-serif typography, carefully aligned 8px spacing, thin neutral rules, subtle 8px radii, near-black #17171e left nav, soft-white #faf9fc workspace, pale lilac #eee8ff selection and #b8a2ed primary button. Restrained semantic amber/red for urgency, no generic statistic cards or charts.

Layout: 190px-wide dark sidebar; header spanning the main area; below a 540px-wide operational request queue and a spacious selected request detail pane. Strong hierarchy and generous but efficient whitespace. Left nav only "Requests" selected, "Progress", "Contractors", "Settings", with simple consistent outline icons and small compact MetroNest monogram.

Header heading "Maintenance requests", small subtitle "Review issues. Approve the next step." and Sample data chip. Queue toolbar tabs "All 4", "Urgent 1", "Ready 1", "Waiting 2"; four compact beautifully spaced rows with clear labels and small status tags. First row selected in pale lilac: "Plumbing request", "Unit 8 · King Street", ID "MN-DE4280", status "Ready", priority "High". Three other fictional sample rows "Heating inspection" / "Park Road" / "Waiting"; "Faulty extractor" / "Station View" / "Waiting"; "Door repair" / "Victoria Court" / "Open". Do not fabricate fake revenue or KPI charts.

Selected detail: eyebrow "MN-DE4280 · WEB CHAT"; large "Plumbing request" and amber "High priority" label. Address "Unit 8, 14 King Street" / "Manchester M1 6EU". Section "Triage summary": "Potential damage or service disruption. Confirm tenant access before dispatch." Section "Rough price band" with large "£260–£700", small "Indicative only. Contractor quote takes precedence." Show compact recommendation card "Recommended contractor" / "RapidPipe Plumbing", small "Plumbing · Same-day contact". Plain-English "Recommended action" / "Approve contractor contact and confirm tenant access." In bottom decision area show one clear primary lilac button "Approve contractor", secondary text button "Request more details". Directly nearby show an explicit human approval control: "Auto-approval off" and "Approval limit £650". Use the threshold as an editable-looking field, not a claim the request is auto-approved. A discreet footer note "Requests over £650 need approval." Everything must be readable, short and spelled exactly as provided. No additional unsupported features, no invented logos, no random lorem ipsum. A polished software tool that a senior product engineer would proudly ship. Complete image with no accidentally cropped text.
source: maintenance.webp — pre-existing user-supplied portfolio screenshot used for workflow and factual reference.
intent: Interface redesign concept using sample data. Presentation asset only; not a screenshot of an updated underlying application.
processing: Converted generated PNG to WebP quality 94 with smart subsampling; original dimensions retained.
review: Visually inspected primary labels, cost figures, composition and image edges. Sample data label is visible. Existing source image retained.
